title: Frames Mastery: ROWS, RANGE, GROUPS
objective: After this lesson you will be able to choose correctly among ROWS, RANGE and GROUPS frames; write running and moving aggregates with explicit bounds; use EXCLUDE to drop peers, ties, or the current row; and predict frame behavior on duplicate ORDER BY values.
why: Frames are where window beginners plateau: running totals work, then moving averages misbehave on duplicate dates, then RANGE does something mysterious. The three frame modes exist precisely for peer-tie semantics — physical positions (ROWS), logical peers (RANGE), group-aware spans (GROUPS) — and choosing wrong silently shifts numbers. Mastery here is what separates primer graduates from analysts.

blocks.text: **ROWS** counts row positions: `ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` always covers exactly 3 rows (or fewer at edges). Predictable, fast, and wrong whenever ties matter — two developers with identical hours get different running values depending on arbitrary tie order. Use ROWS for position-defined spans (last 3 enrollments, moving average of N readings).

blocks.code:
-- 3-row moving average of hours (real SQLite/PostgreSQL)
SELECT name, hours_studied,
  AVG(hours_studied) OVER (
    ORDER BY hours_studied DESC
    ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS moving_avg3
FROM developers
ORDER BY hours_studied DESC;
blocks.caption: ROWS: exactly N physical rows, ties split arbitrarily

blocks.text: **RANGE** groups by ORDER BY *value*: `RANGE BETWEEN 100 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` covers peers whose value falls in [current−100, current] — ties included together, always. Same-tied rows share identical frames, so results are tie-deterministic where ROWS is not. Price: the engine must handle value ranges (and SQLite restricts RANGE offsets to a single ORDER BY expression — know your engine's frame limits).

blocks.code:
-- Peers within 100 hours: ties travel together (real SQLite/PostgreSQL)
SELECT name, hours_studied,
  COUNT(*) OVER (
    ORDER BY hours_studied
    RANGE BETWEEN 100 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS peers_within_100
FROM developers
ORDER BY hours_studied DESC;
blocks.caption: RANGE: value-based peer sets — deterministic under ties

blocks.text: **GROUPS** (PostgreSQL; SQLite support varies by version — verify before relying) counts *peer groups*: `GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` covers the current tie-group plus the previous tie-group whole. It is the precision tool for ranked data — 'this tier plus the tier above' — where ROWS would split a tie group mid-span and RANGE would over-include by value.

**EXCLUDE** removes frame parts: `EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW` (peers only — 'average of everyone else'), `EXCLUDE TIES` (peers plus current, dropping fellow ties), `EXCLUDE GROUP` (everything but the current tie group). 'How do I compare against others, not myself?' is an EXCLUDE question — and self-comparison bias in leaderboards is the business reason it exists.

blocks.code:
-- Average of *other* developers in the same role (real PostgreSQL; SQLite: verify GROUPS/EXCLUDE support)
SELECT name, role, hours_studied,
  AVG(hours_studied) OVER (
    PARTITION BY role
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
    EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW
  ) AS others_avg
FROM developers;
blocks.caption: EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW: the peer baseline without self-bias

blocks.title: Engine variance lives here
blocks.text: Frames are the least uniform window feature: SQLite historically limits RANGE offsets and GROUPS/EXCLUDE availability varies by version; PostgreSQL is complete. Test every frame construct on your actual engine version (the verify script pattern from this course's repo does exactly this) — never assume from documentation of another engine.

blocks.query: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS n FROM developers GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
blocks.note: Run this tie census in the sandbox — Japan appears twice (the dataset's tie), while hours_studied has zero duplicates. That contrast is the point: ties decide frame behavior, so census tie structure before choosing ROWS vs RANGE vs GROUPS.

items: ROWS positions (ties split) · RANGE values (ties travel) · GROUPS peer-groups (tiers as units)
EXCLUDE sculpts frames: CURRENT ROW out for peer baselines, TIES/GROUP for tier logic
Moving aggregates need explicit frames; defaults depend on ORDER BY presence (Ch.1)
Frame support varies by engine/version — verify constructs, never assume

exercise.prompt: (a) In the sandbox, run the tie census (expect exactly one duplicate: Japan ×2) and confirm hours_studied has zero duplicates with the same query shape. (b) In real SQLite/PostgreSQL, write: (i) 3-row moving average (ROWS); (ii) peers-within-100 count (RANGE); (iii) per-role others-average (EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, full frame). (c) State in one sentence what zero hour-duplicates implies for ROWS-vs-RANGE on hours ordering (identical results), and where the difference would surface instead.
hints: Tie census first: Japan ×2 proves ties exist in this data, zero hour-dupes proves the hours ordering is tie-free — every frame answer below is checkable against that structure.

(i) ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW over ORDER BY hours DESC. (ii) RANGE BETWEEN 100 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW over ORDER BY hours (ascending reads naturally). (iii) PARTITION BY role, full UNBOUNDED frame, EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW.
The one sentence for (c): with zero hour-ties both modes agree on hours ordering — the divergence lives wherever ties exist (Japan pair under country ordering: ROWS splits it, RANGE keeps it whole).
exercise.why: Ties-first methodology: census, then constructs, then the contrast sentence. Frame choice follows from tie structure — the exercise makes the dependency explicit instead of theoretical.

quiz.q: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW vs RANGE with the same bounds on tied data — difference?
options: ROWS takes exactly 3 physical rows (ties split arbitrarily); RANGE takes all peers in the value band (ties travel together)
ROWS is an error with ties
quiz.explain: Positions vs values: ROWS counts slots, RANGE counts peer values. Tied rows share RANGE frames and split ROWS windows — the core frame decision.

quiz.q: Leaderboard 'average of everyone else in my role' needs?
options: Full-partition frame with EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW — otherwise self-bias infects the baseline
quiz.explain: Plain partition averages include the subject row. EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW removes exactly one row — self — leaving the peer baseline. Self-comparison bias is a business bug, not a syntax one.

quiz.q: GROUPS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW is ideal for?
options: Tier-above logic on ranked data — whole peer groups as units, never splitting ties
quiz.explain: GROUPS counts peer groups: current tier plus exactly one tier above, ties intact. ROWS would split a tied tier mid-span; RANGE would over-include by value.

quiz.q: Your frame construct works in PostgreSQL but errors in SQLite. Response?
options: Frame support varies by engine/version: verify constructs on the actual engine, rewrite with supported equivalents (often ROWS), and note the variance
quiz.explain: Frames are the least uniform window feature. Professional practice: test on target versions, prefer portable ROWS where semantics allow, document engine-specific constructs.

summary: ROWS positions, RANGE values, GROUPS tiers — plus EXCLUDE sculpting and explicit-frames-always discipline. Ties decide the mode; engine versions decide availability; verification decides truth.
